content:
Hi there,

We currently have a typeclass Ring.DimensionLEOne which describes rings in which all nonzero prime ideals are maximal. This is not quite what I would expect from a typeclass called DimensionLEOne, as the rings satisfying this are rings with krull dimension 0 and domains with krull dimension 1. As such, I think we should change the name, but I'm not entirely sure what name to suggest. I'm thinking maybe Ring.NonZeroPrimesMaximal, but would be interested in peoples' suggestions (or arguments for why we shouldn't change the name).
I think we've had this discussion before and agreed that the name was lousy
Ah gotcha. In that case, do you have any feelings about what we should change the name to?

From my conversations with @Andrew Yang, it seems that in most cases docs#Ring.DimensionLEOne should be replaced by docs#Ring.KrullDimLE. But of course that shouldn't prevent a better rename in the meantime.

Should we not just get rid of this typeclass and use Ring.KrullDimLE 1 instead? It is true that they are different, but do we care about this class of rings (i.e. things that are either one-dimensional domains or zero-dimensional rings)?
Yeah I don’t personally care about this funny class of rings so I would also be happy with just getting rid of it
This seems somewhat related to #37619
We were discussing whether it made sense to have a class for topologies generated by clopen sets or whether we should just use something like SmallInductiveDimLE 0

I'm considering doing a refactor to get rid of DimensionLEOne following this discussion, and I'm wondering how much we care about IsDedekindRing. This is a concept that exists in the literature, and all the references I can find use the definition in DimensionLEOne (that all nonzero primes are maximal). So, to refactor this definition in terms of Ring.KrullDimLE in a way that preserves the meaning being encoded here will likely involve some ugly hack. However, it's unclear to me how much we care about this notion (there are currently 9 declarations mentioning IsDedekindRing). Do we want IsDedekindRing in mathlib? If so, is this an argument for keeping DimensionLEOne?

I think we do want IsDedekindRing because it's in the literature even though it's a silly idea. However I don't think this is an argument for keeping something whose name is in the literature ("ring of dimension at most one") but which means something else.

Raphael Douglas Giles said:

there are currently 9 declarations mentioning IsDedekindRing

There are currently 650 declarations mentioning IsDedekindDomain, and its definition relies on IsDedekindRing.

Yongle Hu said:

Raphael Douglas Giles said:

there are currently 9 declarations mentioning IsDedekindRing

There are currently 650 declarations mentioning IsDedekindDomain, and its definition relies on IsDedekindRing.

This is of course true, and indeed we should certainly not get rid of IsDedekindDomain. My claim is rather that I think it would be fairly simple to cut out the middle man and just define IsDedekindDomain using IsDomain and Ring.KrullDimLE directly

The name is wrong and the module docstring is wrong (both are mathematically inaccurate) so something needs to be fixed and the sooner the better. People have been discussing privately that what distinguishes mathlib from AI-generated output is that mathlib has a very high level of trust and we need to keep it this way.

I like Andrew's idea of replacing it with KrullDimLE 1 which has none of these problems

Kevin Buzzard said:

I like Andrew's idea of replacing it with KrullDimLE 1 which has none of these problems

This still leaves the question of how IsDedekindRing should be defined. IIUC @Raphael Douglas Giles says that the literature has the condition "every non-zero prime ideal is maximal", which is not equivalent to KrullDimLE 1 in the non-domain case.
You could just write it out, right? And then add an instance for the domain case.

Artie Khovanov said:

You could just write it out, right? And then add an instance for the domain case.

Yeah we can definitely do that, but I think there is already a strong case to be made that this is a typeclass that will (should?) never really be used outside of the domain case, and I think that further disconnecting it from other natural typeclasses by writing this condition out without reference to KrullDimLE or something else which naturally appears elsewhere only makes this case stronger
I think we agree yeah
Ah right sorry yes, I think I misunderstood

To clarify:
I'm suggesting writing out ∀ I : Ideal R, I ≠ 0 → I.IsPrime → I.IsMaximal in the definition of IsDedekindRing R, and then proving instances [IsDomain R] [KrullDimLE 1] : IsDedekindRing R and [IsDomain R] [IsDedekindRing R] : KrullDimLE 1.

Gotcha, my point was that I think this change sort of guarantees IsDedekindRing won't really ever get used, which imo is a good thing but potentially it's better to just do away with IsDedekindRing altogether
right I see
I don't know enough about the maths or Mathlib to speak to that sorry
